messages:
Rita - DevEx: Heads-up: noticed Python sampleapp loses x-request-id and traceparent after an auth-retry. Flow: client -> 401 -> token refresh -> retry. First attempt has headers, retry doesn't. Otel auto-instrumentation + contextvars in use. Anyone run into this?

Noah - SDK: is the retry done by requests.Session or a custom wrapper? requests' built-in adapters usually preserve headers, but people often rebuild the PreparedRequest.

Tess - SampleApps: sampleapp uses requests + a tiny wrapper around session.send to handle refresh. Here's the simplified retry path from sampleapp: ```py
def send_with_retry(prepared):
    resp = session.send(prepared)
    if resp.status_code == 401:
        refresh_tokens()
        new_req = requests.Request(prepared.method, prepared.url, data=prepared.body)
        prepared2 = session.prepare_request(new_req)
        return session.send(prepared2)
    return resp
```

Rita - DevEx: so prepared.headers got lost because they didn't copy over headers into new_req. OK. But curious why otel/contextvars didn't re-inject trace headers on retry. Shouldn't OTEL http instrumentation re-run propagation?

Jordan - Infra: Auto-instrumentation hooks often run when the request is prepared/sent, but if you reconstruct a brand new Request without the context carrying propagator headers, and if the instrumentation only adds propagation during initial injection (or you disabled inject_on_retry), headers can be missing. Also contextvars in Python are per-task; if refresh runs in a new thread or subprocess, context can be lost.

Noah - SDK: two angles: (A) sampleapp bug: don't rebuild request without headers; copy prepared.headers or re-use PreparedRequest; (B) SDK/otel: add a safety check that when outgoing HTTP has neither traceparent nor x-request-id we emit a WARN and include a hint. Could be a config flag to spam less.

Tess - SampleApps: quick repro script I used: ```bash
XID=r-xyz curl -i -H "x-request-id: $XID" -d '{"t":"x"}' http://localhost:8000/api/gen
```
and logs showed: 
```
INFO  incoming headers {"x-request-id": "r-xyz", "authorization": "Bearer a"}
WARN  auth -> refresh
INFO  outgoing headers {}
```

Rita - DevEx: Also found weirdness with the sampleapp's redact config in config.yaml: somebody added a redact regex `.*id.*` for a tenant demo which will happily match x-request-id. That would remove it from logs but not from the outgoing request object. Two different failure modes.

Jordan - Infra: good catch. Could be both: missing in outgoing request and also masked in logs if redact rules match. Recommend: 1) change redact regex examples to avoid greedy patterns; 2) warn in docs about not using `.*id.*` globally; 3) ensure sampleapp test covers both cases.

Noah - SDK: I opened rwd.issue/1512 to track: add a one-time WARN in our http instrumentation when an outgoing request is sent without propagation headers but the incoming context has a trace id (we can compare). Also add an opt-in strict mode that fails CI for sampleapps.

OpsBot: CI check: sampleapp v0.7.2 on staging uses old retry impl, failing trace continuity test 3/5.

Tess - SampleApps: I'll push fix: change new_req = requests.Request(...) to copy headers: `requests.Request(prepared.method, prepared.url, headers=dict(prepared.headers), data=prepared.body)` and add a unit to assert 'x-request-id' present in spans. PR -> https://rwd.in/pr/4781

Rita - DevEx: tiny docs note for onboarding: under "HTTP retries" add bullet: "When implementing retries, prefer re-sending PreparedRequest or ensure headers+contextvars are copied. See sampleapps/python-gen retry example."

Jordan - Infra: ops follow-up: add an integration test in infra-tests that triggers 401 path and asserts trace continuity across refresh. Non-negotiable for sampleapp CI.

Noah - SDK: also thinking about telemetry: emit a metric `sdk.propagation.missing_on_retry` with labels (lang=python, sampleapp=true|false) when detected. That will let us spot regressions in the field.

Tess - SampleApps: PR created with fix + test + docs. Running local unit, passes. Will request review.

Rita - DevEx: tl;dr: root cause was rebuilding request without headers + tenant redact regex possible interference. Fix landed in sampleapp PR, SDK issue logged for instrumentation warning, infra test added to backlog. Closing once PR merged. :white_check_mark:
